statement.p: Use the linear approximation to estimate
Compare with the value given by a calculator and compute the percentage error:

static.solution:
(0.99)^{2}(1.01)^{2} is a value of the function f(x,y)=x^{2}y^{2}.
We use the linear approximation at the point (1,1), which is f(1+h,1+k) \approx f(1,1)+f_x(1,1)h+f_y(1,1)k We compute the value of the function and its partial derivatives at (1,1): \left. \begin{array}{lcl} f(x,y)=x^{2}y^{2} \amp \amp f(1,1)=1 \\ f_x(x,y)=2xy^{2} \amp \Rightarrow \amp f_x(1,1)=2 \\ f_y(x,y)=2x^{2}y \amp \amp f_y(1,1)=2 \end{array} \right.
Substituting these values gives the approximation
f(1+h,1+k)\approx 2h+2k+1 We substitute h=-0.01, k=0.01 to obtain (0.99)^{2}(1.01)^{2} \approx 1 The absolute value of the actual value given by calculator is |f(0.99,1.01)|\approx 0.9998.
The error is 0.00019999 and the percentage error is \frac{0.00019999}{0.9998}\times 100\%=0.020003 \%
